title: Renewal & Expansion Check-in - Silverpine Finance
meeting_header:
Date: 2026-06-03
Start: 15:00 PDT
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Alex Ruiz (Redwood CSM); Tom Alvarez (Silverpine), Meera Patel (Silverpine), Luis Gomez (Silverpine), Nadia Chen (Silverpine Security)
summary: Quarterly renewal and capacity expansion check-in. Customer is evaluating additional Dedicated GPU capacity (4x -> 8x), adding EU region (Frankfurt) for data residency, and extending contract term for a better rate. Discussed performance expectations, benchmark plan, security artifacts (SOC 2, VPC/KMS), and next steps for pricing and a pilot benchmark run.
transcript:
[00:00] Jordan Lee: hey everyone, thanks for joining on short notice uh i'll kick us off. this is jordan from redwood, ae for silverpine. quick roll call?
[00:12] Tom Alvarez: tom here.
[00:15] Meera Patel: meera on the line.
[00:18] Luis Gomez: luis, procurement.
[00:20] Nadia Chen: nadia, security.
[00:22] Priya Nair: priya from redwood infra, hi.
[00:25] Jordan Lee: great. goal for today is to discuss your upcoming renewal, the requested capacity bump, and the region add. we want to make sure timelines align and that we have a benchmark plan.
[00:38] Meera Patel: yeah thanks. high level - renewals up in 30 days, current commit is 4 gpus reserved (we call them 4x) for production inference. we've been hitting limits during peak trading windows and want to explore doubling to 8x dedicated for steady throughput. also compliance needs require an EU region for european customers.
[01:00] Priya Nair: okay sounds familiar - app is low-latency critical? what's the p50/p95 you're seeing now?
[01:07] Meera Patel: p50's fine ~80-100ms for 1k token prompts but p95 spikes to 420ms when cache misses happen during bursts - those bursts are when we fall back to smaller batch routes and latency jumps.
[01:20] Jordan Lee: got it. that maps to what we saw in the instrumentation. the dedicated pool will help with predictable throughput; doubling to 8x buy you more concurrent streams and heavier KV cache residency.
[01:32] Tom Alvarez: question on cost - doubling capacity doubles commit cost right? we need to justify ROI to finance.
[01:38] Jordan Lee: correct baseline cost doubles, but that's where contract term & pricing tiers come in. if you extend to a 12-month or 24-month term we can tier pricing and offer effective per-token reductions; also our optimize tools can reduce unit costs with batching and prefix caching, so net spend increase could be less than linear.
[01:58] Luis Gomez: can you send the draft numbers? finance needs line items.
[02:02] Jordan Lee: yes i'll share updated pricing sheet after this call.
[02:05] Nadia Chen: on the EU region: our compliance team needs to confirm data residency, encryption at rest with customer KMS, and audit logs retention. do you support customer-managed KMS in the private control plane?
[02:17] Priya Nair: yes - for Private deployments we integrate with customer KMS/HSM; for Dedicated we support customer KMS via our VPC peering and key wrapping. i'll follow up with the specific deployment topology doc - there was a small naming quirk in the doc where we said "Redwood Dedicate" in the older PDF, sorry about that.
[02:38] Meera Patel: ha, noted. can you confirm SOC 2 + ISO artifacts?
[02:42] Jordan Lee: SOC 2 type II report and ISO attestation are available; we'll send the most current package.
[02:48] Priya Nair: also for the EU region, there are network egress considerations if you keep data in eu-west vs eu-central. we recommend frankfurt for your partners.
[02:59] Tom Alvarez: timeline - we'd like frankfurt up within 6 weeks if possible. realistic?
[03:03] Priya Nair: six weeks is tight but doable for hosted + dedicated pool provisioning; we'll need to schedule capacity and a short maintenance window. if you want private install on-prem that's longer.
[03:13] Meera Patel: one more technical - during spikes we see cache thrash; any kernel/quantization suggestions? our models are 7b mixed-precision.
[03:24] Priya Nair: for 7b models the best win is quantization to int8 or dynamic 4-bit profiles; additionally our runtime has smarter kv cache residency and continuous batching. we can run a quick benchmark with your sample workload to surface exact latency/cost tradeoffs.
[03:43] Jordan Lee: would you prefer we run the benchmark in your dev account or in our managed sandbox?
[03:48] Meera Patel: dev account, we want to replicate network egress and auth behavior.
[03:52] Priya Nair: fine. Meera can share a short workload spec and keys; we'll coordinate with infra to run the benchmark using your data patterns.
[04:01] Tom Alvarez: on contract extension - our procurement prefers a 12-month extension in exchange for a 10% discount, plus a 30% discount on incremental capacity. is that something you can consider?
[04:12] Jordan Lee: we can definitely consider structured discounts for term + incremental commit. i'll work with finance but 10% baseline for 12 months might be tight; 24-month gets better rates. the 30% on incremental capacity is plausible - we often do step-up pricing for additional reserved pools.
[04:28] Luis Gomez: please get us a formal amendment we can review.
[04:31] Jordan Lee: yes, will do.
[04:33] Nadia Chen: security question on audit logs - retention for 12 months is required and logs must include token-level request metadata stripped of user PII. can you confirm?
[04:43] Priya Nair: we can retain request metadata 12+ months in our console; for PII we have redaction options and can stream audit logs to your SIEM via secure syslog or s3 with encryption.
[04:55] Meera Patel: perfect.
[04:58] Jordan Lee: ok to recap: 1) Jordan -> send updated pricing + draft amendment for 8x capacity and term options (12/24 months). 2) Priya -> share deployment topology + KMS/VPC docs. 3) Priya & Meera -> schedule benchmark run in Meera's dev account for week of June 8. 4) Jordan -> send SOC 2/ISO package and security addendum. 5) Alex Ruiz (CSM) to coordinate rollout timeline and onboarding checklist. any additions?
[05:25] Tom Alvarez: add: procurement needs lead time for billing changes - we need final numbers by June 10 to approve in next finance meeting.
[05:33] Jordan Lee: noted, we'll aim for June 5 on pricing so you have 5 days.
[05:38] Meera Patel: one more - do you have any reference architecture for multi-region failover? we'd like redirection and auto-failover, plus fallback to smaller cheaper models if region is down.
[05:48] Priya Nair: yes our smart routing supports region preference / fallback to hosted variants; i'll attach a design doc. there's a small caveat: automatic model variant fallback requires compatibility settings - we'll show examples.
[05:59] Nadia Chen: also please include SAML SSO integration steps for our internal users.
[06:03] Jordan Lee: will include.
[06:05] Luis Gomez: thanks everyone. procurement will review the amendment once received.
[06:08] Jordan Lee: great thanks. we'll follow up with artifacts and schedule the benchmark.
[06:12] Tom Alvarez: thanks all. bye.

Note: transcription includes some auto-caption errors e.g., "Redwood Dedicate" instead of "Redwood Dedicated" and occasional speaker attribution glitches.
